title.context: The guide page: heading, and its name in Settings → Help.

intro.message: How to use the app day to day, in the order you'll need it. "Show me" opens the screen and points at the spot.
intro.context: Guide page: line under the heading. Keep "Show me" matching guide.show.

show.context: Guide: button on a step that opens its screen and highlights the element.

optional.context: Guide: marks a getting-started step that can be skipped.

doneLabel.context: Guide: accessible label of the check mark on a finished step.

todoLabel.context: Guide: accessible label of an unfinished step.

progress.context: Guide: progress of the getting-started list. Both are numbers.

allDone.message: All set up. The rest is habit: the sections below.

open.context: Settings → Help: button that opens the guide.

when.context: Guide section: when you do it.

categories.message: {settings} → {categories}: rename, add ({newCat}) or hide categories so they match how you really spend, and give each a monthly limit.
categories.context: Guide, getting started. Placeholders are app labels, shown in bold.

accounts.message: {savings} → {newAccount}: add every savings account, deposit, IKE/IKZE/PPK or bonds with {balanceToday}, so the app starts from real numbers.

emergency.message: {newGoal} "Emergency fund" with {emergency} switched on (or open a goal you have → Edit). Aim for 3 to 6 months of spending.

debts.message: {newDebt}: every loan, card or mortgage with {owedToday}, its interest and monthly payment. No debts? Skip it.

regular.message: {budget} → {regular}: add the subscriptions and the bills that come back (insurance, car service, taxes) with how often and when they're next due.

billsFund.message: Make a goal for those bills (e.g. "Bills") and switch {billsFund} on in it: the app then says whether it holds enough.

income.message: Log this month's pay: the round ↑ button ({addIncome}) at the top of {add}.
income.context: Guide, getting started. Keep the ↑ arrow: it's how the button looks.

plan.message: Plan this month on {budget}: see "At the start of the month" below.
plan.context: Guide, getting started. The quoted name must match guide.month.title.

ai.message: {settings} → {aiCard}: paste a free Gemini key to turn on the recommendations, plan drafts and {askAi}.

phones.message: On every phone: open the site → Share → Add to Home Screen, sign in once, and say whose phone it is.
phones.context: Guide, getting started. Use the phone's own wording for Share and Add to Home Screen.

when.context: Guide section: when you do it.

expense.message: {add}: tap a category, type the amount (or tap the quick amounts), {saveExpense}. Right after paying is easiest.

yesterday.message: Forgot one? On the amount screen pick {yest} or a date before saving.

goal.message: Paid from savings (a trip, a repair from the emergency fund)? Tap the {goals} tile and pick the goal: it stays out of the month's budget and comes off its account.

fix.message: A mistake? {history} → tap the entry to change the amount, date or category, or to delete it.

borrowed.message: Someone else paying from your phone? Tap the name on the amount screen to log it as theirs.

when.context: Guide section: when you do it.

log.message: Tap ↑ ({addIncome}) on {add}, type the amount, {saveIncome}. Pay that arrives near the month's end can count for the next month ({paysFor}).

oneOff.message: Money that won't come again (a deposit back, something sold): mark it {oneOff}, so it doesn't inflate your typical pay.

paycheck.message: Saving pay opens {paycheck}: pay in each line (goals, IKE, loan instalments) before you start spending. It's also on {budget}.

title.message: At the start of the month
title.context: Guide section heading. guide.start.plan quotes it.

when.message: Once a month, 10 minutes, ideally together
when.context: Guide section: when you do it.

review.message: In the month's first week {budget} shows how last month went: what went over and what was left. Look before you plan.

plan.message: Tap {planMonth} (or the badge by the month). Start from last month's plan or {fillTypical} spending, then adjust each limit.

zero.message: Make it come to zero: income − savings − limits = 0, so every złoty has a job. The planner says what's still unassigned.

savings.message: In savings, give each goal its line (the chips say what it needs to be on time, and how much the bills fund needs), and pick where last month's leftover goes.

ai.message: Not sure? {aiDraft} suggests limits from a year of your spending; nothing changes until you tap a suggestion.

when.context: Guide section: when you do it.

safe.message: {add}: the number at the top is what's really free to spend this month. Below zero means slow down.

warnings.message: {budget} shows which categories are close to or over their limit: react now, not at the month's end.

debt.message: After a loan instalment: {savings} → the debt → {update} → {instalment}.

ask.message: Questions like "can we afford a holiday in July?": {askAi}.

when.context: Guide section: when you do it.

subscriptions.message: {budget} → {regular}: when it says {reviewNow}, go through the subscriptions and cancel what you don't use.

balances.message: IKE, IKZE, PPK, bonds, investments: {savings} → the account → {updateBalance} to what the statement shows. The difference is your gain.

debtBank.message: Debts: {update} → {bank} with the balance from the bank, so the estimate stays accurate.

bigPicture.message: Look at {netWorth} on {savings} and {fire} on {insights}: are they moving the right way?

when.message: When you wonder how you're doing

health.message: {health} on {budget}: savings rate (20% or more), fixed costs (under half the income), emergency fund (3–6 months), age of money (30 days or more). The red one is the one to work on.

netWorth.message: {netWorth}: what you have minus what you owe. With a mortgage it's below zero for years; what matters is that it climbs.

debtPlan.message: {debtPlan}: dearest first saves the most interest, smallest first gives quick wins. Any extra a month shortens it.

fire.message: {fire}: 25 years of spending lets you live off your savings. Spending less helps twice: a smaller target, and more saved.

allowance.message: Money nobody has to explain: {settings} → the category → {whose} → one person. Only their phone shows what's in it.

fixed.message: Rent and bills: switch {inChart} off in the category. They stop crowding the chart and count as fixed costs.

borrow.message: Something urgent? {savings} → {assistant} → {borrow}: take it from savings and pay it back in instalments every plan puts aside.

together.message: Plan the month together and agree on the limits: a budget works when everyone in it says yes to it.
